Question Inspired by a recent article posted to v/technology... Just as the title states, what jobs will automation kill next and which jobs are safe?
Voaters, what jobs will automation kill next and which jobs are safe?

As soon as they become road legal, self driving cars are going to put taxi drivers, bus drivers, and long haul truckers out of business. Pretty much nobody with a CDL will be safe.

As far as safe jobs go, I would go with medicine. Developed countries tend to accrue a surplus of elderly people and there's no technology that can replace the human factor.

Not to mention I wouldn't trust a computer to diagnose me. I could input my symptoms all day but as a non-medical professional I wouldn't even know where to start looking for things besides the most obvious stuff. Pretty sure it's not lupis.

I hope they become a thing, but I really wonder if they will. The liability issues seem like they would be crippling. Some accidents are unavoidable even for super amazing robot cars, so when they do inevitably happen who is responsible?

Fast food. Already you can order from a terminal and the drinks machines automatically dispense the drink. It's only a small step now to a self assembling burger line. There will be one person to tend to the machines and keep up stock

There are already machines that make burgers.

Momentum Machines cofounder Alexandros Vardakostas told Xconomy his "device isn’t meant to make employees more efficient. It’s meant to completely obviate them." Indeed, marketing copy on the company's site reads that their automaton "does everything employees can do, except better."

http://www.businessinsider.com/momentum-machines-burger-robot-2014-8

Manufacturing is already largely automated. I work on the distribution end of brakes/chassis production and I could see where even that could possibly be automated by way of a sophisticated mechanical catalog system in our warehouse.

Emergency services will remain safe. People can't deal with technology when they're losing their minds in an emergency situation. They need someone to (sometimes forcibly) tell them what to do. Machines are a long way off from that kind of respect or authority.

I'd imagine plumber, electricians, etc. have pretty safe jobs. I think that even though there's tons of online material for learning, teachers will have safe jobs too.

I think waiters/waitresses might be in trouble except maybe at those really fancy restaurants. I know a few restaurants in my area have tablet things at the table that you can order with.
Its not really automation but the more reliable Windows is getting the less I have to do as an ICT administrator.

Often, the automation doesn't get you let go, it gets you displaced. If you make Widget X, and there are 12 lines, and they upgrade from 200 weiget Xs a minute to 1500, you are going to need support personnel to handle all the additional productions. Also, if youre a good operator, its easy to work yourself into a quality position.

If your job is repetative, or requires no deep thought, its probably in trouble. Automation is only currently replacing the lowest thought positions.

Landscapers, maids, Human interface jobs, skilled trades, business positions etc are relatively safe because its more of an art.

Robots can't exactly move around cleaning things... Yet.

As someone mentioned, self driving cars impacting trucking, I'd say thats a pretty safe bet. An algorithm could be devised using GPS to put a truck into position on a dock, and remove it and provide it to a truck.
